open_points.subject: viewer read-only authority versus lazy budget creation
open_points.text: “Viewer capabilities are read-only; a viewer can never mutate data” versus “reading the progress of a project that has no budget yet creates its empty manual budget version, also for an archived project”
open_points.question: When a viewer reads progress for an archived project with no budget, does that read create persistent budget state despite the viewer’s read-only invariant, or is creation limited to another actor or system authority?
options: Every authorized progress reader, including a viewer, causes creation
Only a staff reader causes creation
The system creates it independently of the reader’s authority
Viewer progress reads do not create it
open_points.default_guess: Treat creation as a system-owned side effect permitted for every authorized progress reader.

witness.initial: An archived project has a viewer grant, progress is readable, and no budget exists.
events: The authenticated viewer requests the project’s progress.
outcomes: The request persists an empty manual budget attributed to or triggered by the viewer.
The request remains strictly read-only and does not create a budget.
witness.observer: The viewer on a later budget read and an administrator inspecting stored budgets or audit records

open_points.subject: meaning of no budget yet
open_points.text: “a project that has no budget yet”
open_points.question: Which stored state satisfies “no budget yet”: no budget versions of any kind, no manual version, no active version, or no client-visible budget?
options: No manual or imported budget version exists
No manual budget exists, even if imported snapshots exist
No budget version is active
No budget is currently client-visible
open_points.default_guess: Require that no manual or imported budget version exists.

witness.initial: An archived project has an imported snapshot but no active budget version and no manual budget.
outcomes: An empty manual budget is created because there is no active budget.
No manual budget is created because a snapshot budget version already exists.
witness.observer: Staff reviewing the project’s budget versions

open_points.subject: state of the created empty manual budget
open_points.question: What facts and lifecycle state does creation establish, especially whether the version is active, client-visible, and the project’s sole current budget?
options: Create and automatically activate a client-visible empty manual version
Create an inactive manual version
Create a special initialization record that is not an ordinary budget version
open_points.default_guess: Create and atomically activate an ordinary empty manual budget version.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget.
events: An authorized actor reads progress, causing the stated creation.
The viewer subsequently requests the budget summary.
outcomes: The viewer sees an active manual budget with no sections.
The viewer still sees budget data as unavailable because the created version is inactive or not an ordinary budget.

open_points.subject: concurrent lazy budget creation
open_points.text: “reading the progress … creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: If multiple progress reads concurrently observe no budget, must they converge on exactly one empty manual budget version, and what happens to losing attempts?
options: Exactly one version is created and every read succeeds against it
Multiple inactive versions may be created but at most one becomes active
One read succeeds and competing reads fail or retry
open_points.default_guess: Enforce one version per project for this initialization and let all reads succeed against it.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget and is visible to two authorized sessions.
events: Viewer B requests progress concurrently before A’s creation commits.
outcomes: One empty manual budget version exists after both successful reads.
Two empty manual budget versions exist, or one request fails with a conflict.
witness.observer: The readers and staff inspecting budget-version history

open_points.subject: failure of progress read during lazy budget creation
open_points.text: “reading the progress … creates its empty manual budget version”
open_points.question: If the progress data can be read but the empty budget cannot be persisted, does the read fail, return progress without creating the budget, or return another explicit unavailable result?
options: Fail the entire progress read with a storage error
Return progress and leave the budget absent
Return an explicit progress-unavailable result
open_points.default_guess: Fail the entire read so the promised creation and response are atomic.

witness.initial: An archived project has readable progress and no budget; storage reads work but a budget write fails.
outcomes: The viewer receives the progress while no budget is created.
The viewer receives a storage-unavailable failure and no progress.

open_points.subject: audit of read-triggered budget creation
open_points.text: “reading the progress … creates its empty manual budget version” versus “Every significant action records actor provenance” and the inclusion of “budget changes” in audit
open_points.question: Is this lazy creation audited as a budget change, and if so which principal and action are recorded when a read caused it?
options: Audit a budget-creation action attributed to the reader
Audit a system action that references the triggering reader
Treat lazy initialization as non-significant and record no audit
open_points.default_guess: Audit the budget creation with the authenticated reader as actor and a distinct lazy-initialization action.

witness.initial: An archived project has no budget and an authorized viewer can read progress.
events: The viewer reads progress and an empty manual budget is created.
An administrator reviews the audit trail.
outcomes: The audit contains a budget-creation record with actor provenance.
No audit record exists because the operation was nominally a read.

open_points.subject: bootstrap success-message delivery boundary
open_points.text: “the success message shows the normalized email to the operator who supplied it” while the email is otherwise “never printed, logged or audited”
open_points.question: Through which output channel is the normalized email shown, and is command output captured by a process supervisor or deployment log still permitted?
options: Write it to standard output even if the host captures that stream
Write it only to an attached controlling terminal
Return it through another operator-only local channel
open_points.default_guess: Write it to the controlling terminal and avoid ordinary captured output streams.

witness.initial: The first administrator does not exist and the bootstrap command is run by a deployment supervisor that captures stdout and stderr.
events: The host operator supplies an email and password.
The command succeeds and emits its success message.
outcomes: The normalized email is written to stdout and becomes part of the deployment log.
The email is shown only on the operator’s terminal and is absent from captured logs.
witness.observer: The host operator and anyone with deployment-log access

open_points.subject: viewer-entry rate limit
open_points.question: What attempts share the viewer-entry limit, what threshold and time window apply, and what observable failure is returned when it is exceeded?
options: Limit by source address
Limit by access-link credential or viewer
Limit by both source and credential
Apply one deployment-wide limit
open_points.default_guess: Limit by both source address and credential, with a concealed rate-limit failure.

witness.initial: A valid viewer access link exists and has not been revoked.
events: An attacker makes repeated invalid entry attempts from one address.
The legitimate viewer then uses the valid link from another address.
outcomes: The legitimate entry succeeds because limits are isolated by source.
The legitimate entry is refused because attempts against the credential or a global bucket exhausted its limit.
